title: Studio settings tab shows the controlled_by_parent refusal verbatim: ADR reference and English text reach end users
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

Filed as a `finding` by seat `repo:objectstack#2` from the #36512 dev's report (card comment 7082981555, `open_questions[1]`), relayed by area s2-C. Not triaged; not claimed.

## What

`packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts` builds the `controlled_by_parent` refusal messages with an ADR citation in the text. The citations are at lines 231, 248 and 288 on `main`: "ADR-0055 §1: since @objectstack/spec 18, a controlled-by-parent object derives its master from …".

The Studio object settings tab shows this message verbatim. That is the intended design of objectui#12326: the refusal is the author-facing explanation. So when an author picks "controlled by parent" on an object with no usable `master_detail` field, the page shows:

- an internal ADR reference, which a metadata author has no reason to know, and
- English text on a zh UI, because the message is not localised.

## Why it matters

The message reaches end users of Studio, not only lint or CLI output. An ADR section number is a developer citation, not product copy, and the untranslated text breaks the zh surface.

## Where the fix likely lands

`domain:spec` (the message text and any message code a UI could localise from), possibly with a ui half that renders a localised string keyed by a code instead of the raw text. The fix is not decided here. PR for #36512 does not touch spec and only names this in its Acceptance notes.

## Re-check

`grep -n "ADR-0055 §1" packages/spec/src/data/controlled-by-parent-master.ts` (non-zero hits on message lines = still present).
